answer: Every hollow anchored in the forge loses half its voting capacity each epoch unless re-bought, and the n-th renewal the forge sells in an epoch costs n/100 timber on a public curve that resets each epoch. The forge fingerprints each hollow's judged outputs, so near-duplicate clones collide there and are voided. An honest agent renewing among 1,000 others pays about 10 timber an epoch, while a farm keeping 1,000 extra hollows live burns about 15,000 more timber every epoch, forever. It breaks if timber is cheap or renewals can be bought off-curve.
